title: Vrooli Resource Manifest
description: Manifest schema for manifest-driven resource control plane resources.

storage.description: Portable declaration of the resource's on-disk storage surface.

retention.description: Declared storage ceilings for the runtime data this resource accumulates. Enforced by packages/api-core/retention. Distinct from durable_data, which declares what to back up.

execution.description: The execution-plane contract for a coding-agent resource. install_only resources are intentionally provisioned but not runnable by agent-manager.

cli.description: Installed artifact contract for the resource CLI, including build/install/invoke/freshness semantics.

legacy_repo_data_allowed.description: Temporary escape hatch for retained resources that still rely on repo-local data paths.

durable_data.description: Durable host-filesystem state this resource accumulates that is worth backing up (e.g. an external-cli coding agent's conversation history). HOST-FILESYSTEM ONLY: container/compose resources store volume data captured separately by data-backup-manager's live connectors and MUST NOT declare it here. Consumed by data-backup-manager discovery to surface one-click backup target suggestions; entry contents are never read.

base.description: Host directory the entries are relative to. Supports a leading $HOME, ~, or %USERPROFILE% token (resolved to the operator's home directory). Defaults to $HOME when omitted. Slash-normalized.

host_only.description: Always true today: durable_data describes host-filesystem state only. Reserved for a future non-host declaration kind.

entries.description: Durable entries under base, keyed by stable logical name (the key becomes the suggested target name).

managed_service.description: Authority and provider-selection contract for a Vrooli-owned local service. This declaration never grants lifecycle authority over an external endpoint.

provider_policy.description: Verified reuse policy for a non-service host tool. It never grants process lifecycle authority.

acceleration.description: The single accelerator declaration. Replaces the deprecated gpu block, requirements.gpu, and the top-level capacity block.

backends.description: Ordered backend preference. The last entry is the floor the resource can always fall back to.

require.description: required fails install and start when no declared non-CPU backend is ready; preferred falls through and records mode drift; none makes the accelerator opportunistic.

cuda.description: Configuration used when the cuda backend is selected.

min_compute.description: Minimum vendor compute capability as a decimal string. Replaces requirements.gpu.min_cuda_compute.

compose_overlay.description: Compose overlay layered on when this backend is selected, relative to the resource root or absolute.

env.description: Environment applied to the resource process when this backend is selected.

verify.description: Overrides how the control plane reads observed placement for this backend.

kind.description: Evidence source. Absent selects the default for this backend and placement target.

device.description: Narrows a device check to one device-node family.

library_paths.description: Directories the dynamic loader must search for this backend's shared libraries, relative to the staged artifact or absolute. Acquisition verifies the artifact's runtime closure against them.

requirements.description: Declared resource footprint used by deployability resolution. Values are authored inputs, not computed verdicts.

privilege.description: Host privilege needed to operate this resource outside a desktop bundle.

bundling.description: Whether the resource may be supplied by a desktop application bundle.

host_ip.description: Optional host interface address for Docker port publishing, rendered as host_ip:host:container. Leave empty to bind all interfaces.

kind.description: Semantics of the check. readiness (the default interpretation) must fail until the resource can serve its primary capability, including model/data load; liveness means process-alive only.

memory_limit.description: Optional cap passed verbatim as `docker run --memory <value>`. Format: positive integer optionally suffixed b/k/m/g (case-insensitive), e.g. "12g", "8192m", "536870912".

dependency_schema.description: Resource-specific schema fragment for scenario dependency declarations under dependencies.resources.<name>.

startup_budget.description: Optional driver-owned readiness budget that grows from an observed unit count; the declared lifecycle timeout remains the floor.

deployment.description: Resource-owned deployment profiles. A supported claim requires declared target evidence and, for bundled modes, a prebuilt CLI artifact contract.

upstream_cli.description: External CLI (e.g. claude, codex, opencode) this resource wraps. Records the pinned version and docs source so config adapters can detect upstream schema drift via `permissions doctor` / equivalent surfaces.

version_command.description: argv used to report the upstream CLI's version (e.g. ["claude", "--version"]).

version_pinned.description: Upstream CLI version the adapter was authored against. doctor warns when the installed version diverges.

docs_source.description: Canonical upstream docs URL the adapter's config schema was derived from.

docs_pinned_at.description: Date the docs URL was last reviewed (ISO 8601 date).

schema_version.description: Bumps when the adapter's on-disk state schema changes incompatibly.

companions.description: Host-side companion processes the compose-service driver supervises alongside the container.

operator_capabilities.description: Operator capability references this resource satisfies.

portability_tier.description: Declared portability tier for this resource.

runtime_env_command.description: CLI invocation whose KEY=VALUE stdout is appended to the compose process environment.

artifact_role.description: Release manifest role for the staged service artifact.

provenance_class.description: Release manifest provenance label declared by the resource.

target_defaults.description: Runtime-specific defaults. Control-plane hosting uses a Vrooli-owned shared service; desktop bundles start private unless shared reuse is explicitly selected and consented.

shared_reuse_requires_consent.description: A desktop app must obtain explicit consent before it joins a user-level shared instance.

external_management.description: External endpoints are attach-only: Vrooli may validate and use them but never initializes, unseals, stops, or rewrites them.

external_access_capabilities.description: The only application access that an attach-only external provider may request. This never grants lifecycle authority.

artifact.description: An immutable executable staged beneath the resource or bundle root. The release pipeline verifies its signed checksum set; the lifecycle driver verifies this SHA-256 before launch.

layout.description: Artifact verification/launch layout; directory artifacts use the declared entry_path and tree digest.

entry_path.description: Executable path relative to a directory artifact root.

bundle_artifact.description: Target template for the separately signed server asset included in a bundled-service release (for example vault_${os}_${arch}).

verification.description: Use host-tool only when acquisition.kind=none explicitly adopts a separately governed PATH tool; staged artifacts remain checksum-verified.

acquisition.description: Declared source, verification, and host-fact selection contract for the managed-service artifact.

attach_health_path.description: Health request path used only when an operator explicitly selects attach-only provider mode.

arguments.description: Literal argv passed directly to the verified executable. Shell interpolation is never performed.

environment.description: Literal environment values supplied only to the managed process. Secrets are not permitted here; resolve them through provider-scoped credentials.

credential_files.description: Authority fields materialized as owner-restricted, short-lived files below RESOURCE_STATE_DIR; never environment or argv values.

executable_by_platform.description: Per-target bootstrap executable, relative to the staged tree, for platforms whose archive layout or executable suffix differs.

arguments_by_platform.description: Per-target bootstrap argv that replaces arguments entirely for the named platforms.

bootstrap.description: One idempotent initialization command run from the verified directory artifact when the marker is absent.

process_limits.description: Limits applied by the managed-service supervisor to the launched process.

signal.description: Platform-neutral first shutdown request. terminate is SIGTERM on Unix; interrupt is SIGINT on Unix and the native console-control request on Windows.

shutdown.description: First shutdown request for the supervised process. The resource lifecycle stop timeout bounds graceful waiting and triggers forced escalation if needed.

arguments_by_platform.description: Per-target argv that replaces arguments entirely for the named platforms. Keys are "os" or "os-arch"; the exact os-arch key wins. A platform difference belongs here rather than in a runtime.GOOS branch in the driver.

capacityClaim.description: Capacity broker claim. A vram claim must declare a degrade profile and yield_when_idle, otherwise the broker can never step the resource down.

profile.description: The adopter-declared degradation ladder, ordered preferred to floor.

verb.description: Resource CLI verb the broker invokes to ask for a step down.

argv.description: Argument vector; may contain the {label} placeholder.

upshift.description: Whether the broker may raise the resource back up when capacity frees.
